regions.name: Hawaii
regions.summary: Warm, clear water year-round, green sea turtles almost everywhere, and many free shore entries.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: An underwater scene showing a sea turtle and several tropical fish swimming around a mo... by Faisal Ahammad · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Green sea turtles on the sand at almost every beach
Coral reefs that start within a few hundred yards of shore
Warm water all year, from 78F in January to 84F in August
regions.wetsuit_note: No wetsuit. Hawaii runs 78-84F (26-29C) all year, so a rash guard is the most useful thing to bring, for sun rather than for cold.
rules_do: Keep 10 ft (3 m) from green sea turtles
Use reef-safe sunscreen
Respect the Marine Life Conservation District rules posted at each site
rules_avoid: Do not touch or stand on coral
Do not feed fish or turtles
Do not take shells or any marine life

regions.name: Southern California
regions.summary: Kelp forests, bright orange garibaldi and summer leopard sharks in cool, protected marine reserves.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: California Coast by philgear · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Orange garibaldi in the kelp forests of Catalina
Summer leopard shark aggregations at La Jolla Shores
Marine reserves covering most of the Southern California coast
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm full suit most of the year: the water sits around 60-64F (16-18C). A 2mm shorty is enough from July to September, when it reaches 68F (20C).
rules_do: Stay inside the marine reserve boundaries
Keep your hands off the kelp and the rock
Pack out everything you carry in
rules_avoid: Do not take any marine life, including urchins, abalone and rockfish
Do not feed fish or sea lions
Do not swim in a closed rookery

regions.name: Florida
regions.summary: The only living coral barrier reef in the continental US, plus manatee springs.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Panorama of a Key West beach in Florida by David Orban from Italy · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: The only living coral barrier reef in the continental United States
Manatee and spring runs that hold 68-72F all year
Sea turtles nesting on uncrowded beaches from May to October
regions.wetsuit_note: Ocean: a 3mm shorty or rash guard from November to March, when the Gulf drops to 70-75F (21-24C). Springs: skin or a 1mm suit, because the water never drops below about 68F (20C).
rules_do: Check for stingrays and shuffle your feet in shallow sand
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from turtles and manatees
Fly a dive flag on any boat snorkel in state waters
rules_avoid: Do not take coral, sponges or any marine life
Do not stand on coral
Do not feed wildlife or block a turtle's path to the surface

regions.name: Big Island
regions.summary: Kona's lava-rock coves, the Captain Cook Monument reef and the famous manta ray night snorkel.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: File:Female scuba diver swims with a young male Manta ray - Kona district, Hawaii.jpg by Steve Dunleavy from Lake Tahoe, NV, United States · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: The manta ray night snorkel in Kona
Sea turtles basking at dawn on the black sand at Punaluu
A flooded cave at Kaue, reached on a 2-mile round trip
regions.wetsuit_note: No wetsuit: 78-84F (26-29C) all year. A rash guard and reef shoes for the lava entries are enough.
rules_do: Float at the surface at night and let the mantas come to you
Give turtles space when they are basking
Go to Kealakekua Bay early, because the hike is hot and exposed
rules_avoid: Do not touch the turtles on the black sand
Do not land on the islet at Molokini
Do not take marine life inside the reserves

regions.name: Maui
regions.summary: Molokini Crater by boat, and calm reef coves from Kapalua to Makena that you can walk into.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: File:Green Sea Turtle, Maui.jpg by Bernard Spragg. NZ · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Molokini Crater, a sunken volcanic caldera snorkelled by boat
Green turtles at Makena Beach, where the reef runs close to the sand
Calm reef coves at Kapalua and Kuilima
regions.wetsuit_note: No wetsuit: 78-84F (26-29C) all year. A rash guard for the sun, and reef shoes for the lava shelf at Makena.
rules_do: Snorkel Makena at low tide, when the reef is shallow and clear
Keep to the marked swim zones
Book Molokini trips for a calm morning
rules_avoid: Do not land on Molokini, because it is a seabird sanctuary
Do not stand on the coral or take shells
Do not feed the fish

regions.name: Oahu
regions.summary: Free shore coves on the North and West shores, Hanauma Bay by reservation, and turtle boats off Waikiki.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Snorkelers with sea turtle (Kahaluu Bay) by Vlad & Marina Butsky · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Lanikai Beach's calm, shallow reef and its turtles
The tide pools at the far east end of the island
Hanauma Bay's protected coral, for the days you want a guide and a fee
regions.wetsuit_note: No wetsuit: 78-84F (26-29C) all year. Bring a rash guard and a reef shoe for the lava entries at Makapuu.
rules_do: Use a rash guard, because the sun is the real risk on an exposed reef
Keep to the posted swimming areas
Park early at Lanikai, because the lot fills by mid-morning
rules_avoid: Do not enter the Makapuu tide pools alone, because sharks are present
Do not take coral or shells
Do not step on coral to reach a better view

regions.name: Catalina Island
regions.summary: A ferry ride from LA to kelp forests and marine conservation areas right off Avalon.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Paysage de laminaires à Molène (Ifremer 00753-86498 - 44333) by Olivier Dugornay (Ifremer) · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Kelp forests that run from the beach into the channel
Sea lions hauled out on the rocks at Casino Point and Camp Cactus
A marine reserve that covers the whole south end of the island
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm full suit is the standard here: the Catalina Channel runs 60-64F (16-18C) most of the year. Snorkelers wear one even on a calm July day.
rules_do: Keep well back from resting sea lions and seals
Stay on the trail at Little Eggs Beach
Use reef shoes for the rock entry
rules_avoid: Do not enter the closed marine mammal rookery at Little Eggs Beach
Do not take marine life: the whole island is a no-take reserve
Do not swim alone; the channel builds current quickly

regions.name: San Diego
regions.summary: La Jolla's underwater park: garibaldi at the Cove and leopard sharks off the Shores in summer.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: California coast (36618554403) by Dale Cruse from San Francisco, CA, USA · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Garibaldi fish grazing in the kelp at La Jolla Cove
Leopard sharks in the warm shallows from June to October
The La Jolla Shores tidewalk along a protected kelp bed
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm full suit for most visits: La Jolla water runs 62-66F (16-19C). From July to September a 2mm shorty is usually enough.
rules_do: Walk on the sand at the tidewalk and step off it to swim
Shuffle your feet when you walk on the sand
Keep at least 10 ft (3 m) from leopard sharks
rules_avoid: Do not swim off the Scripps pier: rips run around the pilings
Do not touch or stand on the kelp bed
Do not take abalone, urchins or any marine life

regions.name: South Florida
regions.summary: Miami, Lauderdale-by-the-Sea and the Florida Keys sit on one continuous shelf of coral and mangrove coast. It is also the heart of Floridas shallow-water recovery work, where outplanted staghorn and elkhorn are rebuilding a nursery that the rest of the reef depends on.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Underwater scene off the coast of Humacao, Puerto Rico by edskoch · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Coral patch reefs in Biscayne National Park by boat
A natural three-tier reef 100 yards off a street-end beach in Lauderdale
The reef tract that starts at the sand and runs 21 miles off the Keys
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm shorty from November to March, when the water sits at 72-75F (22-24C). A rash guard is enough from May to October.
rules_do: Fly a dive flag on any boat snorkel
Keep a wide berth from the boat channel
Stay inside the marked swim zones in Biscayne National Park
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or marine life anywhere in the Keys reef tract
Do not touch the wrecks or the trail markers
Do not swim in the marked channels

regions.name: Florida Springs
regions.summary: Cold, clear water that has never seen sunlight rises from the Floridan aquifer and surfaces through dozens of springs. Each one holds close to 72 degrees all year, which makes them the best-value diving in Florida once the ocean gets cold.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Snorkeling Playa Funchi, Bonaire (12841334175) by SNORKELINGDIVES.COM · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Water that holds 68-72F all year because it never sees sunlight
Wild manatees in the colder months
Clear spring runs you can swim for a mile
regions.wetsuit_note: None needed. The water sits at 68-72F (20-22C) all year, so a swimsuit is more comfortable than a wetsuit. Use a 1mm suit only if you are cold-sensitive.
rules_do: Use a float and a snorkel in the spring runs
Stay out of the spring head itself
Pack out everything, because there is no current to carry it away
rules_avoid: Do not feed or touch manatees, and never approach a calf
Do not swim above the spring pool, where the current is strong
Do not bring glass into the water

regions.name: Florida Keys
regions.summary: An eighty-mile arc of coral, mangrove and seagrass where the reef runs from the beach out to the deep blue. This is the only reef in the continental United States that starts at the sand, and the only place a snorkeler can watch the shelf drop away from the shore.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Interdependencies of coral reef, seagrass and mangrove ecosystems by Earp, H.S., Prinz, N., Cziesielski, M.J. and Andskog, M. · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: The only reef in the continental US that starts at the sand
A 21-mile reef tract running from John Pennekamp to the edge of the shelf
Loggerhead turtles nesting on the Keys beaches
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm shorty from November to March, when the water is 72-75F (22-24C); a rash guard or skin from May to October, when it reaches 85F (29C).
rules_do: Fly a dive flag: it is required by state law
Stay on the marked snorkel trail at John Pennekamp
Carry water, sunscreen and a cover-up, because the reef gives no shade
rules_avoid: Do not spearfish or take coral anywhere in the Keys sanctuary
Do not touch the Seven Mile Bridge stumps or cut off barnacles
Do not swim in the Dry Tortugas moat

regions.name: Lauderdale-by-the-Sea
regions.summary: A small barrier-island town nine miles north of Miami, where a street-end beach portal opens onto a natural three-tier reef about 100 yards offshore and a 2002 shipwreck snorkel trail runs over a British steamship broken up in the 1970s.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Coral Reef aerial by Photo courtesy of Sean Connolly. · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: A three-tier natural reef that starts about 100 yards from a street-end beach
The 2002 Shipwreck Snorkel Trail over the broken-up SS Copenhagen
Turtles and schooling fish on a reef most people can reach from shore
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm shorty from November to March, when the water sits near 72F (22C). Most people snorkel without one from May to October.
rules_do: Look for the yellow marker buoys and keep the trail in sight
Watch for boats and give divers room at the reef
Park legally and use the beach portal at the end of Datura Avenue
rules_avoid: Do not touch the wreck pieces, the anchor or the cannon
Do not take any artefact or marine life
Do not enter the marked channel

regions.name: Miami
regions.summary: Coral patch reefs and wrecks in Biscayne National Park by boat, plus easy beaches on Key Biscayne.
regions.hero_image_credit: Photo: Sunset In Key Biscayne Miami Florida Travel Photography by Giuseppe Milo · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
highlights: Biscayne National Park reefs with wild coral and large fish
A shallow, sandy bottom at Crandon Park for beginners
Patch reefs and wrecks a short boat ride from the city
regions.wetsuit_note: A 3mm shorty or rash guard is enough from May to October. From December to March the water drops to 72-75F (22-24C) and many snorkelers wear one.
rules_do: Check the tide and wind before you leave the beach
Use the free three-hour parking passes at Crandon Park
Watch the channel markers and stay on the ocean side
rules_avoid: Do not take shells or coral
Do not feed the fish
Do not swim in the inlet or the marina channel

spots.name: Honolua Bay
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Roadside pull-offs on Honoapiilani Highway, then a short trail through the forest.
spots.getting_there_text: North of Kapalua on Honoapiilani Highway (Hwy 30).
spots.depth_text: Reef along both sides of the bay
spots.best_season_text: Summer. In winter the bay is a big-wave surf break.
spots.seasonal_warning: Winter swells make it unsafe, and water turns murky after rain.
spots.hazards_text: Rocky entry; check for surf before going in.
spots.protected_area_name: Honolua-Mokuleia Bay Marine Life Conservation District
spots.rules_text: No taking of marine life inside the MLCD.
spots.summary: A wild, forest-backed bay in West Maui with rich coral and turtles, best on calm summer mornings.
highlights: A deep, clear reef pool with a coral wall
Dense fish schools in a sheltered cove
A Marine Life Conservation District with no take at all
spots.natural_features: A rocky inlet with a coral reef on the outer wall and a sheltered sandy pool inside.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard in summer. A 3mm shorty for the winter months, when the water drops to 72-74F (22-23C).
spots.water_temp_note: 72-80F (22-27C), coldest in February and March, warmest in August and September.
rules_do: Check the surf and the swell before entering, because the bay breaks hard in winter
Stay on the rock and the sand edge and move out on the reef
Use reef shoes for the entry
rules_avoid: Do not take any marine life: it is an MLCD
Do not touch the coral
Do not feed the fish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: A large sand tiger shark swims majestically over a colorful coral reef in a deep blue a... by Faisal Ahammad · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Honolua Bay is one of the oldest Marine Life Conservation Districts in Hawaii, established in 1953, which makes it one of the earliest no-take areas in the state.

spots.name: Waialea Bay (Beach 69)
spots.getting_there_text: On the Kohala Coast north of the Waikoloa resorts.
spots.depth_text: Coral close to shore
spots.best_season_text: Mornings, year-round.
spots.summary: A shaded Kohala Coast beach with coral and turtles close to shore, calmest in the morning.
highlights: A shallow bay with a sandy bottom
Turtles in the shallows at the north end
A quiet alternative to the busier north coast spots
spots.natural_features: A sand and shallow reef bay with a rocky point and a small fringing reef.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and the bay is calmest in the morning.
rules_do: Snorkel the reef at the north end of the bay
Walk on the sand where the bottom is shallow
Give the turtles space
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or shells
Do not feed the fish
Do not stand on the reef
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: (Aerial view of coastline on Hawaii Island, United States) - DPLA - 89b167478c207932509... by Carlquist, Sherwin John, 1930-2021 · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The bay is in a Marine Life Conservation District, where all marine life is protected from take, and the turtles here rest in the shallow water.

spots.name: Maluaka Beach (Turtle Town)
spots.entry_fee_text: Free from shore; boat tours also stop offshore.
spots.parking_text: Free public lot near the beach.
spots.getting_there_text: In Makena, South Maui.
spots.depth_text: Reef along the south end of the beach
spots.best_season_text: Year-round; mornings before the trade winds.
spots.summary: A gentle Makena beach where green sea turtles feed along the reef to the south. Boat tours also stop offshore.
highlights: Turtles resting on the sand in a small cove
A rocky, lava-lined shore
Easy snorkelling from the beach
spots.natural_features: A rocky lava shoreline with a shallow reef and sandy pockets, the traditional turtle resting area on Maui.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Give the resting turtles space and never block their route
Snorkel early, before the boat tours arrive
Stay off the lava rock
rules_avoid: Do not touch or crowd the turtles
Do not take shells
Do not feed the fish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: A school of fish at the Alexander by U.S. Forest Service (source) · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The turtles here are a well-known population, and the site is a Marine Life Conservation District, so nothing can be taken from it.

spots.name: Maunalua Bay
spots.entry_fee_text: Included in the tour price.
spots.getting_there_text: Tours depart Hawaii Kai; some include transport from Waikiki.
spots.depth_text: Shallow and deeper reefs; flotation provided
spots.best_season_text: Year-round.
spots.summary: A broad reef bay east of Diamond Head with daily green sea turtle sightings and only a couple of snorkel tour operators.
highlights: A deep, blue boat-only snorkel
Coral outcrops with large fish
Very few people, because it takes a boat
spots.natural_features: A rocky shoreline with coral outcrops just offshore and deep water close by.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Fly a dive flag
Stay with the boat and keep an eye on the swell
Watch for current in the deeper sections
rules_avoid: Do not take marine life
Do not feed the fish
Do not touch the coral
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Woman snorkelling -San Andres, Archipelago of San Andres, Colombia-9Feb2011 by ...some guy · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The bay is surrounded by a Marine Life Conservation District, which protects the coral and the fish that live on it.

spots.name: La Jolla Cove
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Street parking is limited and often full; paid lots nearby.
spots.getting_there_text: In La Jolla village, about 20 minutes north of downtown San Diego.
spots.depth_text: Kelp and rocky reef from shallow to deep
spots.best_season_text: Late summer and early fall for the warmest water and best visibility.
spots.hazards_text: Swell and surge on the rocky entry. Cold water most of the year: wear a wetsuit.
spots.protected_area_name: Matlahuayl State Marine Reserve (San Diego-La Jolla Underwater Park)
spots.rules_text: No taking of any marine life. Give resting sea lions and seals plenty of space.
spots.summary: A small sandy cove in the San Diego-La Jolla Underwater Park with bright orange garibaldi, kelp and sea lions on the rocks.
highlights: Garibaldi fish and a sea lion colony on the rocks
A kelp forest you can swim right through
The view from the shore that brings people here every day
spots.natural_features: A rocky coastal kelp forest on a shelf of rock and sand, with pinniped haul-out sites above.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit. La Jolla water runs 60-65F (16-18C) most of the year, and the kelp forest holds the cold in.
spots.water_temp_note: 60-68F (16-20C), coldest in February and March.
rules_do: Enter at the sandy bottom on the north side, away from the shore break
Keep well back from the resting sea lions
Go on a calm day, when the surge is low
rules_avoid: Do not take any marine life
Do not feed or approach the sea lions
Do not stand on the kelp
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Plongeur évoluant au-dessus d'algues laminaires à Molène (Ifremer 00753-86499 - 44342) by Olivier Dugornay (Ifremer) · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: La Jolla Cove sits inside the La Jolla Marine Reserve and the San Diego Marine Life Conservation District, both of which prohibit all take.

spots.name: Manta Ray Night Snorkel (Keauhou)
spots.entry_fee_text: Included in the tour price.
spots.getting_there_text: Night boat tours leave from Keauhou Bay and Honokohau Harbor.
spots.depth_text: You float at the surface holding a lit board
spots.best_season_text: Year-round, after dark.
spots.hazards_text: Night ocean conditions; stay with your group and the light board.
spots.rules_text: Float at the surface and keep your hands to yourself; let the mantas come to you.
spots.summary: Reef manta rays feed on plankton drawn to underwater lights while snorkelers float above. Boat tours only.
highlights: Manta rays up to 20 ft wing span, in a group of five or six
A night plankton feed that brings them to the surface
A coral garden lit by torchlight on the way home
spots.natural_features: Open coastal water over a deep reef flat, with coral bommies and the manta aggregation feeding on plankton at the surface.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: No wetsuit: 77-83F (25-28C) all year. A warm layer for after, because the night air drops fast after sunset.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) all year, and the water is often warmer than the air at night.
rules_do: Float on your back and keep your hands to yourself
Keep your torch off the mantas
Stay with the group and follow the light board
rules_avoid: Do not touch the mantas
Do not chase them or try to guide them
Do not use flash photography
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Manta ray swimming freely by U.S. Agency for International Development · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The Hawaiian manta population is monitored by the National Marine Fisheries Service, and the operators work with researchers who identify individuals by their belly patterns.

spots.name: Kahaluu Beach Park
spots.entry_fee_text: Free beach access. Non-residents pay for parking (since December 2022); residents with ID park free.
spots.parking_text: Lot fills early on weekends and cruise-ship days; overflow street parking sometimes available.
spots.getting_there_text: On Alii Drive about 5 miles south of Kailua-Kona.
spots.depth_text: Shallow, reef-protected pond
spots.best_season_text: Year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Rip current at the north end where the reef opens. Stay inside the marked snorkel zone.
spots.rules_text: Stay 10 ft from turtles. Do not stand on coral.
spots.summary: A shallow, reef-protected pond in Kona with turtles almost daily and Reef Teach volunteers on the beach.
highlights: A green turtle pool right at the shore
Two freshwater springs that meet the ocean
A marked swim zone with a lifeguard and a boater boundary
spots.natural_features: A sand and lava shoreline with coral close in and a freshwater spring surfacing under the reef.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year and the shore entry is shallow, so sun is the only thing to dress for.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Stay inside the marked swim zone, which is buoyed and watched by lifeguards
Shuffle your feet in the sand for stingrays
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from the turtles
rules_avoid: Do not stand on the coral
Do not feed the turtles
Do not swim past the buoys into the boat channel
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Underwater Tanning by Tilonaut · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Kahaluu is a Marine Life Conservation District and a Hawaii Marine Laboratory Refuge, and the turtles here are habituated to people but still protected.

spots.name: Two Step (Honaunau Bay)
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. The fee kiosk is for the national historical park, not the boat ramp.
spots.parking_text: Very small. Park outside the national park gate so park visitors have space; fills by midday.
spots.getting_there_text: At the Honaunau Bay boat ramp, next to Puuhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park; the access road is one-way.
spots.depth_text: Lava steps straight into deep water
spots.best_season_text: Calm mornings, year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Boat traffic at the ramp; careful entry and exit on the lava ledges.
spots.rules_text: Do not enter the water at Keoneele Cove inside the park (a cultural site). Do not use park restrooms to change or rinse off.
spots.summary: Natural lava steps drop straight into a clear coral garden next to Puuhonua o Honaunau, with turtles and often spinner dolphins nearby.
highlights: Two submerged lava steps and a rocky shoreline
A marked swim area with a lifeguard on the beach
Clean water and deep blue close to shore
spots.natural_features: Lava ledges stepping down into deep water, with reef and sand patches and a rocky shoreline.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and calmest in the early morning.
rules_do: Enter at the ramp and step carefully over the lava ledges
Watch for boats loading at the ramp and keep clear of the loading zone
Snorkel in the morning, before the trade winds
rules_avoid: Do not enter the water at Keoneele Cove inside the park
Do not take marine life
Do not use the park restrooms to change or rinse off
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Hawaiian Lionfish, Manta Ray Bay, Kailua-Kona, HI, USA imported from iNaturalist photo... by (c) jeyre, some rights reserved (CC BY) · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The area is part of the Kona Coast State Historic Park, and Keoneele Cove at the end of the trail is a cultural site with its own restrictions.

spots.name: Kealakekua Bay (Captain Cook Monument)
spots.entry_fee_text: No park entrance fee; tours are priced separately.
spots.getting_there_text: Hike the steep Kaawaloa Trail from the highway, or join a permitted guided kayak tour or a boat tour from Kona.
spots.depth_text: Shallow coral shelf dropping to deep, clear water
spots.best_season_text: Year-round; calm mornings.
spots.hazards_text: Steep, exposed hike with no restrooms or water. Pack out all trash.
spots.protected_area_name: Kealakekua Bay State Historical Park and Marine Life Conservation District
spots.rules_text: All kayaks, boats and boards need a State Parks permit to cross the bay, and permitted vessels may not land at Kaawaloa Flat. If you rent a kayak, confirm it has a valid bay-transit permit.
spots.summary: Clear, calm water and dense coral below the Captain Cook Monument. Reach it by a steep hike, a permitted kayak tour or a boat.
highlights: A freshwater bay and an ancient heiau on the shore
Coral in the last bay, on the edge of a drowned valley
A hike in, with no road to the water
spots.natural_features: A drowned river valley with coral in the protected interior bay, surrounded by lava rock and old settlement sites.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and the bay is often calmer in the morning.
rules_do: Hike in early: the 2-mile round trip is exposed and there is no shade
Pack out everything, including what you brought in
Stay on the trail past the heiau, which is a cultural site
rules_avoid: Do not touch or take anything from the heiau or the burial caves
Do not take coral
Do not land a kayak without a state permit
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: A serene beach scene with clear blue skies and turquoise water. A red and white jet ski... by Nasim Miah · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The bay contains the Puʻuwai heiau, a sacred site that is protected, and the shoreline is a state historic site with its own rules.

spots.name: Ahihi-Kinau Natural Area Reserve
spots.entry_fee_text: $5 per vehicle for non-residents (card machines in the lot). Free for Hawaii residents, who still display a free pass.
spots.parking_text: Designated stalls only; the lot fills early.
spots.getting_there_text: South of Makena at the end of Makena Alanui Road.
spots.depth_text: Coves and sand channels close to shore
spots.best_season_text: Mornings, when the bay is calm. Skip it when waves roll straight in.
spots.hazards_text: Sharp lava entry: reef shoes required. Most of the reserve is closed to entry.
spots.rules_text: No fishing at any time. Stay in posted areas. Do not touch turtles.
spots.summary: A lava-fringed reserve in South Maui with dense coral, turtles and clear coves. Non-resident vehicle fee; go early.
highlights: Spinner dolphins in the bay at dawn
Dense coral and 400-year-old colonies
A 35-acre protected reserve you snorkel from shore
spots.natural_features: Lava substrate and a living coral reef in a cove that was closed to fishing in 1972 and became a reserve in 1994.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year and the shallow entry means you will be in and out of the sun.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) all year. The reef warms up fast in the sun, so midday is hottest and the wind picks up after that.
rules_do: Keep to the buoyed swim area
Stay on the sand while you are crossing the shallow reef
Let the spinner dolphins come to you
rules_avoid: Do not touch or stand on the coral
Do not feed the fish or the dolphins
Do not swim in the closed section of the reserve
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: delfín tornillo, long-snouted spinner dolphin, spinner dolphin by Gergely Nigg · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The reserve is managed by the Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources, which closes part of it to entry during nesting season. The coral here is some of the oldest in the state and is protected from all take.

spots.name: Olowalu Reef
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Roadside parking near mile marker 14 on Honoapiilani Highway.
spots.getting_there_text: South of Lahaina on Honoapiilani Highway (Hwy 30), near mile marker 14.
spots.depth_text: Long, shallow reef flat with coral heads
spots.best_season_text: Calm mornings, year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Very shallow over the reef at low tide; visibility drops with wind and runoff. Go with a buddy or a guide.
spots.summary: One of Maui's oldest and largest reefs, with turtles and coral heads, reached across a shallow sandy entry.
highlights: A wide, shallow reef you can walk out onto
A long sand beach with a rocky point at the end
An untouched feeling despite being close to town
spots.natural_features: A shallow fringing reef in front of a sand beach, with a rocky point and good visibility in the morning.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, with visibility that drops in the afternoon as the wind and runoff increase.
rules_do: Snorkel in the morning, when the water is clearest
Go with a buddy, because the reef is shallow and the surf is small
Stay on the sand and off the reef flats
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or shells
Do not feed the fish
Do not collect sand
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Ocean Floor V (33712023355) by Joe Lin from New York, NY, USA · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The Olowalu area is part of a Marine Life Conservation District, where the shoreline and reef are protected from take.

spots.name: Kapalua Bay
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Small free public access lot; fills early.
spots.getting_there_text: In Kapalua, at the north end of West Maui's resort coast.
spots.depth_text: Shallow reef on both points
spots.best_season_text: Year-round; calmest in summer.
spots.summary: A sheltered crescent bay with reef on both points, one of the easiest family snorkels in West Maui.
highlights: A calm, sandy beach with a reef on one side
Turtles resting on the sand
Easy entry for the whole family
spots.natural_features: Sand beach with a fringing reef to the north and a rocky point to the south.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and calmest in the early morning.
rules_do: Snorkel the reef to the north of the beach access
Walk on the sand to avoid the shallow reef
Keep your distance from resting turtles
rules_avoid: Do not stand on the coral
Do not take shells
Do not feed the fish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Natural Underwater Frame by Tilonaut · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The Kapalua area includes a Marine Life Conservation District, so all marine life in the coves is protected from take.

spots.name: Black Rock (Puu Kekaa)
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Limited public beach access parking; paid resort parking nearby.
spots.getting_there_text: At the north end of Kaanapali Beach.
spots.depth_text: Wall drops from shallow sand to deeper water
spots.best_season_text: Year-round; calmest in the morning.
spots.hazards_text: Current can be strong around the tip of the point.
spots.summary: A lava point at the north end of Kaanapali Beach with turtles and reef fish along its wall, an easy entry from the sand.
highlights: A steep black lava point that drops straight down
Reef fish in deep blue water right off the shore
Clear water and a strong current on the best days
spots.natural_features: Volcanic lava point and wall, with a hardbottom reef that starts in a few feet of water and falls away quickly.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit. The water runs 62-66F (16-19C) most of the year and the wall is deep enough that you will get cold fast.
spots.water_temp_note: 62-70F (16-21C), coldest in February and March and warmest in August and September.
rules_do: Scramble up the rocks away from the breaking waves and let a set pass before entering
Watch the water and the swell for a clean entry
Keep to the point and do not go around the far side alone
rules_avoid: Do not climb on the wet lava at the wave line
Do not take any marine life
Do not swim alone: the point sets up a rip
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: That S The Spot by Tilonaut · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The point is inside a Marine Life Conservation District, where all marine life is protected from take.

spots.name: Molokini Crater
alt_names: Molokini Shoal Marine Life Conservation District
spots.entry_fee_text: Included in the tour price.
spots.getting_there_text: Snorkel boats depart Maalaea Harbor and Kihei. Morning trips usually have the calmest water.
spots.depth_text: Clear water over a sunken crater rim; deep in the middle
spots.best_season_text: Year-round, mornings.
spots.hazards_text: Open ocean with currents outside the crater. Follow the crew's briefing.
spots.protected_area_name: Molokini Shoal Marine Life Conservation District
spots.rules_text: Boat access only. Landing on the islet is prohibited (seabird sanctuary). No feeding fish and no taking marine life.
spots.summary: A crescent-shaped sunken crater off South Maui with famously clear water, reached only by boat.
highlights: A submerged volcanic crater, open on one side
Hundreds of fish in one small place
Turtles that come to rest inside the crater
spots.natural_features: A drowned volcanic caldera with a coral rim, steep inner walls and a sandy floor.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year, and the crater walls shade you from the sun.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Follow the crew's briefing about the currents at the crater mouth
Fly a dive flag
Keep your hands off the coral wall
rules_avoid: Do not land on the islet: it is a seabird sanctuary
Do not feed the fish
Do not take marine life
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Coral Reef off S.E. Molokai Coast ≡ Eric Tessmer, Molokai, Hawaii - panoramio by Eric Tessmer · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Molokini is a state-designated marine life conservation district and a seabird sanctuary, with restoration work and monitoring of the coral and the nesting birds.

spots.name: Turtle Canyon
spots.entry_fee_text: Included in the tour price.
spots.getting_there_text: Snorkel boats and catamarans leave from Waikiki and Kewalo Basin.
spots.depth_text: Offshore reef; tours provide flotation
spots.best_season_text: Year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Open water; stay with the crew and use the flotation provided.
spots.summary: An offshore reef where green sea turtles visit a cleaning station, reached only by snorkel boat or catamaran from Waikiki.
highlights: A coral canyon you can swim along
Turtles resting on the coral below
A boat-only site with clear, deep water
spots.natural_features: A coral ridge and canyon system on the outer reef, with vertical walls and ledges covered in coral.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Use the flotation the crew provides
Stay with the group, because the current runs along the canyon
Fly a dive flag
rules_avoid: Do not take marine life
Do not touch the coral walls
Do not feed the fish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: A variety of bright yellow and orange tropical fish swim together in a clear blue aquar... by Faisal Ahammad · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Turtle Canyon is one of the most-visited snorkel sites in Hawaii and is inside a Marine Life Conservation District, so all marine life is protected.

spots.name: Ko Olina Lagoons
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Limited free public parking stalls at each lagoon; arrive early.
spots.getting_there_text: At the Ko Olina resort area on the west side, about 40 minutes from Waikiki.
spots.depth_text: Shallow, calm lagoons behind breakwaters
spots.best_season_text: Year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Calm, but stay inside the lagoon; currents run outside the breakwater openings.
spots.summary: Four calm man-made lagoons behind breakwaters, easy for kids and first-timers, with reef fish along the rock walls.
highlights: A calm, shallow lagoon with fish that never leave
Green turtles resting on the sand inside the breakwater
No current and no boat traffic
spots.natural_features: A man-made coastal lagoon of shallow sand, rock and coral, separated from the open ocean by a rock breakwater.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year and the lagoon never gets deep.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Stay inside the lagoon, because the currents outside the breakwater openings are strong
Keep off the rocks near the openings
Walk on the sand to avoid the shallow coral
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or shells
Do not feed the fish
Do not climb on the breakwater
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: An underwater scene featuring various fish swimming around a rocky backdrop. by Rakesh Lawaju (Racase) · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The lagoons were built to restore fish habitat and they are managed as a refuge where fish can grow without being caught.

spots.name: Electric Beach
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Free lot at Kahe Point Beach Park.
spots.getting_there_text: Across from the Kahe power plant on Farrington Highway, about 40 minutes from Waikiki.
spots.depth_text: Open water over the outflow pipes
spots.best_season_text: Calm mornings, year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Long swim over open water with strong currents. Never snorkel alone; use a float.
spots.summary: A long swim out to warm-water outflow pipes that draw big fish schools, turtles and sometimes spinner dolphins.
highlights: Night snorkel on a kelp forest
Bio-luminescent plankton in the water on some nights
A long open-water swim from the sandy beach
spots.natural_features: Sand bottom dropping to a rocky reef and kelp, the classic La Jolla night snorkel site.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit and usually a hood: the water is 60-64F (16-18C) and it feels colder at night.
spots.water_temp_note: 60-68F (16-20C). Night snorkelling is best on a warm, calm evening.
rules_do: Snorkel with a buddy and never alone
Use a float, because the swim out to the reef is long
Carry a waterproof torch
rules_avoid: Do not touch the kelp
Do not take marine life
Do not swim in the rip near the shore break
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Coral reef and colorful fish from an aquarium by mdburnette · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The kelp forest off Electric Beach is one of the most studied in Southern California, and the city of San Diego protects it as a marine reserve with no take.

spots.name: Kuilima Cove
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Public beach access parking at Turtle Bay Resort; limited stalls.
spots.getting_there_text: At Turtle Bay Resort on the northern tip of Oahu.
spots.depth_text: Shallow, protected by an outer reef
spots.best_season_text: Best in summer; the outer reef shelters the cove most of the year.
spots.seasonal_warning: Winter surf can push surge over the outer reef.
spots.hazards_text: Stay inside the outer reef.
spots.summary: A small cove sheltered by an outer reef at Turtle Bay, one of the calmest snorkel entries on the North Shore.
highlights: A wide, calm sand beach inside the outer reef
Fish held in by the reef
Sunsets over the water with no crowd
spots.natural_features: A pocket of sand and coral reef protected by an outer reef line, with a shallow shore break.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Stay inside the outer reef, where the water is calmest
Walk on the sand at the shoreline
Snorkel in the morning, when the water is clearest
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or shells
Do not feed the fish
Do not swim outside the reef in the swell
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Munching Turtle by Tilonaut · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The cove sits in a Marine Life Conservation District, where all marine life is protected from take.

spots.name: Sharks Cove
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.parking_text: Free parking nearby; fills early on summer days.
spots.getting_there_text: On Kamehameha Highway in Pupukea, about 10 minutes past Haleiwa.
spots.depth_text: Tide pools near shore, deeper water toward the cove mouth
spots.best_season_text: Calm summer days, roughly May to September.
spots.seasonal_warning: Big winter swells (roughly October to April) make the North Shore dangerous. Never enter when waves break into the cove.
spots.hazards_text: Sharp lava rock and surge at the entry. Wear reef shoes.
spots.gear_text: Bring your own or rent in Haleiwa.
spots.rules_text: No taking of marine life inside the MLCD.
spots.summary: A lava-rock cove on the North Shore with arches, tide pools and turtles, flat and clear only on calm summer days.
highlights: Turtles resting in a small rocky bay
A rocky lava entry into clear water
No crowds, even on a busy Oahu day
spots.natural_features: A small bay with lava rock and shallow reef, with a sandy bottom in places and deep blue water close by.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and the bay is calmest in summer.
rules_do: Use reef shoes for the sharp lava at the entry
Go in the morning, before the swell builds
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from the turtles
rules_avoid: Do not take marine life inside the MLCD
Do not stand on the rock or the coral
Do not feed the fish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Snorkeling Playa Funchi, Bonaire (12841334175) by SNORKELINGDIVES.COM · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The cove sits inside the Waimanalo Marine Life Conservation District, which protects the reef and the turtles that rest in it.

spots.name: Descanso Beach
spots.entry_fee_text: Free beach entry; cabanas and food at the beach club cost extra.
spots.getting_there_text: Just past the Avalon Casino, a short walk from town.
spots.depth_text: Rocky edges of a pebbly cove
spots.best_season_text: Summer and early fall.
spots.summary: A pebbly beach-club cove next to the Casino with fish along the rocks and the occasional sea lion.
highlights: A calm, sandy shoreline under the Palos Verdes cliffs
Sea lions on the rocks near the beach club
Open water views toward the Channel Islands
spots.natural_features: Sand and rock shore with kelp beds and rocky reef close to shore, backed by a bluff.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm shorty: the water runs 62-68F (16-20C). Divers wear a full suit year-round.
spots.water_temp_note: 62-70F (16-21C), coldest in February, warmest in September.
rules_do: Watch for the marine mammals resting on the rocks and keep your distance
Snorkel away from the main swim zone for more wildlife
Check the surf before you go in
rules_avoid: Do not take any marine life
Do not feed the sea lions
Do not swim near the rock outcrops where they haul out
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: CSU Channel Islands by Kevin · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Descanso Beach is next to the Palos Verdes Marine Life Conservation District, which protects the kelp and rock habitat just offshore.

spots.name: Casino Point Dive Park
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.getting_there_text: Next to the Avalon Casino building, a short walk from the ferry.
spots.depth_text: Stairs into kelp forest, deepening quickly
spots.best_season_text: Summer and early fall.
spots.hazards_text: Shared with scuba divers; stay inside the dive park and away from boat traffic.
spots.gear_text: Rentals at Catalina Divers Supply at the Casino.
spots.protected_area_name: Casino Point State Marine Conservation Area (No-Take)
spots.rules_text: No-take marine conservation area.
spots.summary: Avalon's underwater park with stairs into a kelp forest, garibaldi, horn sharks and a small wreck.
highlights: A shore entry straight onto a sloping reef
Garibaldi and kelp bass in the shallows
Scuba divers and snorkelers sharing one protected patch
spots.natural_features: A rocky reef shelf with kelp and hardbottom, protected as a shore-accessible dive park.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit: 60-65F (16-18C). Divers on this site wear one in July.
spots.water_temp_note: 60-68F (16-20C), with the coldest water in January and February.
rules_do: Watch for divers and give them room at the entry
Stay inside the dive park boundaries
Move slowly and keep your hands off the rock
rules_avoid: Do not spearfish or take anything inside the no-take park
Do not feed the fish
Do not swim in the marked boat channel
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Plongeur évoluant au-dessus d'un champ de laminaires à Molène (Ifremer 00753-86487 - 44... by Olivier Dugornay (Ifremer) · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The dive park is a no-take Marine Life Conservation District, which means everything inside it is protected from collection.

spots.name: Lovers Cove
spots.entry_fee_text: Free
spots.getting_there_text: Take the ferry to Avalon, then walk east from town along Pebbly Beach Road.
spots.depth_text: Rocky reef and kelp close to shore
spots.best_season_text: Summer and early fall for the warmest water.
spots.hazards_text: Rocky beach entry. Cool water: wear a wetsuit.
spots.protected_area_name: Lover's Cove State Marine Conservation Area
spots.rules_text: No taking of marine resources (hook-and-line fishing is allowed only from Cabrillo Mole). Fish feeding is legal here, but we ask you not to: it changes fish behavior.
spots.summary: A rocky cove just east of Avalon with garibaldi, kelp bass and calm, clear water inside a marine conservation area.
highlights: A rocky cove with deep blue water and a kelp bed
Sea lions and a resident harbour seal
The clearest water on the island in the afternoon
spots.natural_features: Rocky cove with a kelp forest and rock reef, with a sandy bottom that drops away quickly.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit: 60-65F (16-18C). Divers and snorkelers wear one here even in July.
spots.water_temp_note: 60-70F (16-21C), with the best visibility on a calm afternoon.
rules_do: Enter at the rocky edge on the south side, where the surge is gentler
Give the seal and the sea lions space
Keep your hands off the kelp
rules_avoid: Do not take marine resources
Do not feed the fish, even where it is allowed, because it changes their behaviour
Do not disturb the harbour seal
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Grouper in context by ackbahr · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Lovers Cove is inside the Santa Catalina Island Marine Life Conservation District, where fishing for take is restricted and the kelp forest is protected.

spots.name: La Jolla Sea Caves
spots.entry_fee_text: Included in the kayak tour price.
spots.getting_there_text: Guided kayak and snorkel tours launch from La Jolla Shores.
spots.depth_text: Along the cliffs east of the Cove
spots.best_season_text: Summer and fall; calm mornings.
spots.hazards_text: Swell surges into the caves; go with a guide.
spots.summary: Seven sea caves in the cliffs east of La Jolla Cove, best seen on a guided kayak and snorkel tour.
highlights: Sea caves lit from the water
Sea lions in the cave mouth
A kayaker's view of the kelp canopy
spots.natural_features: Sea caves and a rocky kelp forest in the water off La Jolla.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit. The water runs 60-65F (16-18C) and the caves hold the cold.
spots.water_temp_note: 60-68F (16-20C), coldest in winter.
rules_do: Go with a guide: swell surges into the caves
Sit on the outside of the kayak where you can get out fast
Keep your head down and watch for the ceiling in the caves
rules_avoid: Do not touch the cave walls or the marine life
Do not feed the sea lions
Do not go in alone
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Torpedo californica channel islands by Ed Bierman from CA, usa · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The caves and the kelp around them are inside the San Diego Marine Life Conservation District, a no-take area.

spots.name: The ReefLine
spots.getting_there_text: Off South Beach, Miami Beach. Access details pending.
spots.summary: A planned 7-mile underwater sculpture park and artificial reef off Miami Beach, starting with coral-planted concrete cars.
highlights: A nearshore reef line right along the beach
Shallow, clear water for a swim
Sunrise and sunset over the water line
spots.natural_features: A shallow sand and rubble bottom with a nearshore hardbottom reef line, typical of the Miami Beach shore.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 74-84F (23-29C) in summer and 72-76F (22-24C) in winter.
spots.water_temp_note: 72-84F (22-29C), clearest in the morning.
rules_do: Snorkel at high tide, when the reef is covered and clearer
Watch the jet skis and the boats offshore
Keep out of the channel
rules_avoid: Do not take shells or coral
Do not feed the fish
Do not swim in the boat lanes
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: An underwater scene featuring various fish swimming around a rocky backdrop. by Rakesh Lawaju (Racase) · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The nearshore reef is part of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary boundary and is protected from anchoring and take.

spots.name: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
spots.entry_fee_text: $8 per vehicle.
spots.getting_there_text: At the southern tip of Key Biscayne, about 30 minutes from downtown Miami.
spots.depth_text: Shallow, with seagrass and rocky edges
spots.best_season_text: Calm, clear days with light wind.
spots.hazards_text: No lifeguards. Visibility varies with wind and tide.
spots.protected_area_name: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
spots.summary: A Key Biscayne state park beach with easy, low-key shore snorkeling near the historic 1825 lighthouse.
highlights: A shallow, grassy flat with stingrays and rays
Dolphins passing the point in the morning
Easy shore entry with no boats in the water
spots.natural_features: Mangrove shoreline meeting a shallow sand and seagrass flat, with the reef starting a short distance out.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm shorty from December to March, when the Gulf water drops to 70-74F (21-23C). Bare skin is fine in summer.
spots.water_temp_note: 70-84F (21-29C). Winter is the cooler end, summer brings storms that stir the flat and cut the visibility.
rules_do: Walk at the waterline and shuffle your feet for stingrays
Watch for dolphins on the way in
Check the tide before you set out
rules_avoid: Do not take any marine life
Do not feed the rays
Do not swim in the posted closure areas
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Bright tropical beach with turquoise water, white sand, limestone cliffs, and a sailboa... by Faisal Ahammad · CC0 (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The cape sits inside the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, which protects the mangrove fringe and the nearshore flats from anchoring and take.

spots.name: Emerald Reef
spots.getting_there_text: About a mile east of Key Biscayne; go by charter or private boat.
spots.depth_text: 10 to 20 ft
spots.best_season_text: Calm, low-wind days.
spots.hazards_text: Boat traffic; always fly a dive flag.
spots.summary: A shallow patch reef about a mile off Key Biscayne with coral, spadefish and the occasional dolphin, reached by boat.
highlights: A coral reef in deep, clear water
Sharks, rays and big fish in blue water
A site that rewards a boat snorkel
spots.natural_features: Deep reef habitat off a ledge, with a clean wall and open blue water.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit, and a hood if you are staying in the water for a while: 62-68F (16-20C).
spots.water_temp_note: 62-72F (16-22C), warmest in late summer.
rules_do: Fly a dive flag and keep it above the surface
Watch for current, which runs along the ledge
Stay with the boat and tell someone your plan
rules_avoid: Do not take marine life
Do not feed the fish
Do not touch the reef
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Coral Reef aerial by Photo courtesy of Sean Connolly. · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The Emerald Reef is a submerged reef off the San Diego coast that boaters know for its clear water and pelagic life.

spots.name: Biscayne National Park Reefs
spots.entry_fee_text: No park entrance fee. Guided snorkel trips with Biscayne National Park Institute start at $209 (ages 12+).
spots.getting_there_text: Trips leave from the Dante Fascell Visitor Center in Homestead. The reefs are not reachable from land.
spots.depth_text: Patch reefs, shipwrecks and mangroves; snorkel vest provided
spots.best_season_text: Calm, low-wind days; the captain picks the site by weather.
spots.hazards_text: Open water; fins are required and a snorkel vest is worn.
spots.summary: Coral patch reefs, shipwrecks and mangroves in a mostly underwater national park, reached only by boat.
highlights: Coral heads in 8 to 20 ft of water
Large grouper and barracuda in the open water
Mangrove islands and a shallow bay in the same trip
spots.natural_features: A living coral reef on the edge of the shelf, with hardbottom, patch reef and mangrove shoreline habitats.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm shorty from December to April, when the water sits at 72-76F (22-24C). Most trips run in summer, when a rash guard is enough.
spots.water_temp_note: 74-85F (23-29C) in summer, 72-78F (22-26C) in winter.
rules_do: Wear the snorkel vest the crew provides
Stay with the boat and the group
Bring a rash guard and a hat
rules_avoid: Do not feed the fish
Do not touch the coral
Do not take anything from the reef
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: File:Caspersen Beach, Manasota Key, Florida.jpg by Don Miller from Venice, United States · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The park protects more than 175 square miles of coral and mangrove. Its Institute runs the guided snorkel trips, and the reefs are monitored by the National Coral Reef Monitoring Program.

spots.name: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
spots.entry_fee_text: $25 per non-resident aged 13+, plus a 2.35% online fee. Kids 12 and under and Hawaii residents with ID enter free.
spots.reservation_text: Required for non-residents. Opens online 2 days ahead at 7:00 a.m. HST; one booking covers up to 10 people.
spots.parking_text: $3 for non-residents. About 300 spaces, first come, not included in the reservation.
spots.hours_text: Wednesday to Sunday from 6:45 a.m. Closed Monday, Tuesday, Dec 25 and Jan 1.
spots.getting_there_text: About 15 minutes from Waikiki on Kalanianaole Highway (Hwy 72). TheBus route 22 runs from Waikiki.
spots.depth_text: Shallow inner reef; deeper, clearer outer bay
spots.best_season_text: Year-round. Weekday mornings are calmest and least crowded.
spots.hazards_text: In rough water avoid Witches' Brew (right side), Toilet Bowl (left point) and the Molokai Express current near the bay mouth. Outer bay for experienced swimmers only.
spots.gear_text: Snorkel gear rentals on site.
spots.protected_area_name: Hanauma Bay Marine Life Conservation District
spots.rules_text: Every visitor watches a short reef-protection video. No touching or feeding marine life. Reef-safe sunscreen only.
spots.summary: A protected volcanic bay with a calm inner reef, sea turtles and 400+ fish species, 15 minutes from Waikiki.
spots.answer_block: Hanauma Bay is the easiest great snorkel on Oahu, and one of the most protected. It is a volcanic bay on the southeast coast, about 15 minutes from Waikiki, managed as a nature preserve and Marine Life Conservation District. You snorkel on your own from the beach: the shallow inner reef suits beginners, while the outer bay is for experienced swimmers only. Non-residents need a reservation, which opens two days ahead at 7:00 a.m. Hawaii time, and pay $25 per person aged 13 and over, plus a small online fee. Children 12 and under and Hawaii residents with ID enter free. The preserve is open Wednesday to Sunday from 6:45 a.m. and closed every Monday and Tuesday. Expect green sea turtles, parrotfish and more than 400 fish species. Go early: parking has about 300 spaces and is not included in your reservation.
highlights: A 2,000-year-old coral reef inside a volcanic crater
Green sea turtles on the reef in the first years
A shallow inner bay that beginners can walk into
spots.natural_features: A fringing coral reef on the rim of a sunken crater, with a protected inner bay and a deep outer basin.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: No wetsuit. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year, and the bay is hot and shallow, so a rash guard matters more than warmth.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, with the warmest months running a few degrees higher.
rules_do: Watch the mandatory reef-protection film before you go in
Stay inside the inner bay if you are a beginner
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from turtles and keep your hands off the reef
rules_avoid: Do not touch or stand on the coral
Do not feed any animal
Do not use non-reef-safe sunscreen
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Green Turtle Chelonia Mydas by Kris Mikael Krister · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Hanauma Bay was closed for 25 years from 1990 and reopened in 2000 with a paid reservation system, strict rules and a funded education and restoration programme.

spots.name: Punaluu Black Sand Beach
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. There is no entrance fee.
spots.parking_text: Free paved lot with a short paved path down to the beach.
spots.hours_text: Open 24 hours. The freshwater river pool above the beach is closed when the water is unsafe.
spots.getting_there_text: Highway 11 south from Kona to Punaluu, about 90 minutes. Watch for green turtles basking at the roadside park.
spots.depth_text: Shallow; sand, lava shelf and freshwater mixing at the shore
spots.best_season_text: Early morning. Turtles are usually on the sand near dawn.
spots.seasonal_warning: The river above the beach is freshwater and can carry bacteria. Do not swim above the surf line.
spots.hazards_text: Sharp lava rock. There are no lifeguards.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins; water shoes for the lava shelf.
spots.rules_text: Do not touch, stand on or crowd the turtles. Keep the river and the ocean separate and do not swim in the river pool.
spots.summary: A black-sand beach of volcanic cinder where green sea turtles haul out at sunrise.
highlights: Green sea turtles basking on the black sand at dawn
A freshwater stream meeting the ocean
A beach made of volcanic cinder
spots.natural_features: A black sand beach of volcanic cinder and lava, with a coral reef just offshore and a freshwater stream running to the sea.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year, and you will be on the sand at sunrise.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round.
rules_do: Arrive before sunrise, which is when the turtles come up
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from the turtles and never block them
Keep the river and the ocean separate, and do not swim in the river pool
rules_avoid: Do not touch, stand on or crowd the turtles
Do not swim in the river pool
Do not take sand or shells
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park and Coastline (504050) (22277993129) by Robert Linsdell from St. Andrews, Canada · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Punaluu is a nesting area for green sea turtles, with a turtle protection programme that closes sections of the beach at hatching time and runs daily monitoring.

spots.name: Wailea Beach
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. Paid parking at the resorts is optional.
spots.parking_text: Free street parking along the Wailea Path. The resort lots are for guests only.
spots.hours_text: Beach open 24 hours; the county park closes at 10 p.m.
spots.getting_there_text: South of Kihei on the Piilani Highway. The Wailea Path runs along the sand between the resorts.
spots.depth_text: Waist deep over sand; a rocky reef out to about 100 m, then deep water
spots.best_season_text: Best in the morning. Calmest from autumn through spring.
spots.hazards_text: Shallow lava rock and coral; there is no lifeguard on most of the beach.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins. The reef drops off quickly, so stay shallow if you are not a confident swimmer.
spots.rules_text: Do not take coral or shells. No glass containers. Pack out rubbish.
spots.summary: A calm golden-sand beach on the south shore with a rocky reef shelf and a paved path that runs along the waterline.
highlights: A rocky reef shelf on the south shore
A long, quiet sandy beach
Clear water with a lot of coral within reach
spots.natural_features: A rocky reef platform running along a sand beach, with coral outcrops and a shallow inner shelf.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, with the calmest conditions from autumn through spring.
rules_do: Snorkel the reef along the south shore, and stay off the shallow coral
Use reef shoes where the rock comes close to the surface
Snorkel in the morning
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or shells
Do not bring glass containers
Pack out rubbish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: File:Starr-121029-0399-Cocos nucifera-habit view ocean-Launiupoko Beach Park-Maui (2507... by Forest and Kim Starr · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The south shore of Maui is lined with resort beaches and protected reef, and the coral here is monitored by the Coral Reef Institute for the West Hawaii reefs.

spots.name: Makena Beach
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. There is no entrance fee for the beach.
spots.parking_text: Free paved parking at the trailheads. The lot fills by 9 a.m. at weekends and on holidays.
spots.getting_there_text: From Kahului, take the Piilani Highway (Hwy 31) south past Kihei and turn at Makena Road. The beach is a ten-minute walk down a paved path.
spots.depth_text: Waist to head deep over sand, with a shallow reef ledge at the north end
spots.best_season_text: Year-round, best in the morning. Winter swells are noticeably calmer on this side of the island.
spots.hazards_text: Coral and lava rock in the shallows cause cuts. There are no lifeguards.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins. Watch for trade-wind chop in the afternoon.
spots.rules_text: Do not remove coral, rocks or shells. Do not drive onto the sand. Pack out all rubbish.
spots.summary: Big Beach at the end of the road: half a mile of golden sand, a low reef ledge and sunrise over Molokini.
highlights: Green turtles resting in the shallows
A shallow lava reef right at the sand
A long, empty beach with no buildings on it
spots.natural_features: A sand beach backed by lava rock, with a shallow fringing reef and an open ocean beyond.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round. Winter swells are noticeably calmer on this side of the island.
rules_do: Snorkel in the morning, when the water is calmest and the reef is clear
Use reef shoes over the lava rock
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from resting turtles
rules_avoid: Do not remove coral, rocks or shells
Do not drive onto the sand
Pack out all rubbish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Perhentian Kecil, Malaysia, Tropical beach by Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Makena is on the coast of a protected stretch of Maui, and the turtles here rest on the reef in the shallows, so the beach is monitored during nesting season.

spots.name: Manoa Bay
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. Free public parking.
spots.parking_text: Free lot off the highway; it fills quickly at weekends.
spots.getting_there_text: In the North Shore industrial area just north of the airport; follow the signs for the surf park.
spots.depth_text: A shallow reef shelf of about 3-8 ft, with sand beyond
spots.best_season_text: Mornings, year-round.
spots.hazards_text: Reef cuts, and a steep drop-off at the north end. There is no lifeguard.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins. The water often turns green with runoff after rain.
spots.rules_text: Do not stand on the coral shelf. Leave the turtles and rays alone; never ride or touch them.
spots.summary: A sheltered North Shore bay with a shallow fringing reef where rays and turtles feed in the afternoon.
highlights: A shallow fringing reef you can swim over in a few minutes
Spotted eagle rays in the afternoon
Green turtles on the sand in the shallow water
spots.natural_features: A shallow reef shelf of coral and sand, with a sandy shallow bottom and a deeper edge to the north.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and clearest in the morning before the afternoon trades bring runoff.
rules_do: Snorkel early, before the wind and the swell
Stay off the coral shelf and keep your fins up
Leave the turtles and rays alone
rules_avoid: Do not stand on the coral shelf
Do not ride, touch or follow the turtles
Do not feed the fish
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Hilo coastline Big island Hawaii Park (45553417864) by dronepicr · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: The bay sits inside a Marine Life Conservation District, and the eagle rays and turtles that use it are a monitored population.

spots.name: Makapuu Tide Pools
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. Parking at the Makapuu lot is free.
spots.parking_text: Free lot at the end of the access road near Sea Life Park. It fills by 9 a.m. at weekends.
spots.hours_text: Open 24 hours, but the access can be closed after heavy rain when waves wash over the shelf.
spots.getting_there_text: East end of Oahu, about 30 minutes past Hanauma Bay on Kalanianaole Highway (Hwy 72); turn onto the Makapuu access road opposite Sea Life Park.
spots.depth_text: Tide pools are 1-3 ft deep; the reef shelf outside drops to 6-10 ft
spots.best_season_text: Low tide on a calm weekday. Check the Waimanalo tide table before you drive out.
spots.seasonal_warning: The outer shelf takes a direct hit from large swells. Stay in the pools and the inner reef when the surf is up.
spots.hazards_text: Sharks are present here, including tiger shark and oceanic whitetip. Never swim alone, keep a watch on the water, and stay inside the reef.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins. Reef-safe sunscreen. Do not stand on the shelf to look down into the pools.
spots.rules_text: MLCD rules apply: no taking of marine life, no spearfishing, no touching or standing on coral. Read the posted signs at the entrance.
spots.summary: A lava shelf of connected tide pools at the far east end of Oahu, inside the Mokulua marine reserve.
highlights: Natural tide pools at the edge of the Pacific
Sharks in the open water just beyond the reef
A remote shore with no services and no crowds
spots.natural_features: Basalt lava shelves cut into tide pools, with a fringing reef and deep blue water on the seaward side.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year; you will be out of the water in the sun most of the time.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and the pools hold water at every tide.
rules_do: Go at low tide and read the posted rules before you enter
Never swim here alone: tiger sharks and oceanic whitetip are present
Stay on the lava shelf and off the coral
rules_avoid: Do not take marine life or spearfish
Do not touch or stand on the coral
Do not swim past the reef line
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Sea Urchin Shell detail by Nina Matthews from Australia · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Makapuu is inside the Waimanalo Marine Life Conservation District, so all marine life is protected from take, and the tide pools are fragile habitat that breaks easily.

spots.name: Lanikai Beach
spots.entry_fee_text: Free. No parking fee.
spots.parking_text: Free lot at Lanikai Beach Park, about a four-minute walk from the sand. It fills by 8 a.m. at weekends; street parking on Aoloa Blvd is mostly permit-only.
spots.hours_text: Beach open 24 hours. Lanikai Beach Park facilities close at 10 p.m.
spots.getting_there_text: About 30 minutes from Waikiki: take H-1 east to the Kailua exit, or take TheBus 42 to Kailua and walk ten minutes west.
spots.depth_text: Waist to chest deep over sand inside the reef; the outer reef line drops away quickly
spots.best_season_text: Year-round. The calmest and clearest water is from late spring through early autumn.
spots.seasonal_warning: A big winter northerly swell makes the outer reef dangerous; stay inside the lagoon.
spots.hazards_text: Shallow coral heads and lava rock cause cuts. There is no lifeguard at Lanikai, so swim near the wall or with a local.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins. A rash guard is enough in summer; a 3/2 mm wetsuit in January.
spots.rules_text: Do not take coral or shells. Do not stand on the reef. Do not feed the fish. Pack out everything you carry in.
spots.summary: A half-mile of white sand and a long fringing reef fourteen kilometres east of Waikiki, with a small sand island just offshore.
highlights: A shallow, calm reef that beginners can walk into
Green turtles grazing on the reef
An almost unbroken sand beach with the Mokulua islands offshore
spots.natural_features: A fringing reef of coral heads and sand channels a short way offshore, with a wide sand beach and a shallow inner lagoon.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A rash guard. The water is 77-83F (25-28C) all year, and the reef sits in full sun.
spots.water_temp_note: 77-83F (25-28C) year-round, and the clearest from late spring to early autumn.
rules_do: Enter near the middle of the beach, where the reef is shallow
Swim with a local if you are not confident, since there is no lifeguard at the Lanikai end
Keep 10 ft (3 m) from the turtles
rules_avoid: Do not take coral or shells
Do not stand on the reef
Do not feed the fish
Pack out everything you carry in
spots.hero_image_credit: Photo: Shaheed Island, Andaman Islands, Tropical beach by Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY (cropped and colour-graded)
spots.conservation_note: Lanikai is a Marine Life Conservation District, and the beach is one of the most heavily used turtle habitat on Oahu, with daily turtle counts run by volunteers.

spots.name: Camp Cactus
spots.entry_fee_text: Free.
spots.parking_text: Free roadside parking along Catalina Island Road.
spots.getting_there_text: East end of Catalina Island on Catalina Island Road, about three miles east of Avalon.
spots.depth_text: Rocky shore and kelp; the reef runs out to about 20 ft
spots.best_season_text: Summer and early autumn.
spots.hazards_text: Rocky entry and a steep drop-off. Catalina Channel swell can make this a rough place in winter.
spots.gear_text: Mask, snorkel and fins, 3/2 mm wetsuit, water shoes for the rock.
spots.rules_text: No taking of marine life. Keep off the rock and leave the sea lions on the ledges alone.
spots.summary: A quiet east-end Catalina shore dive with kelp, rock and California sea lions drying on the ledges.
highlights: Sea lions on the ledges above the water
A kelp bed and rock reef on the east end
Clear water with a drop-off just past the entry
spots.natural_features: Rocky lava shore with kelp and a steep submarine ledge, the habitat for the island's California sea lion colony.
spots.wetsuit_recommendation: A 3mm full suit: 60-64F (16-18C) most of the year, and the channel can feel colder still when a swell runs.
spots.water_temp_note: 60-68F (16-20C), coldest in winter when the Catalina Channel runs its biggest swell.
rules_do: Give the sea lions plenty of space and keep off the ledges
Enter where the rock is lowest and the surge is smallest
Watch for the Channel swell before you commit to the water
rules_avoid: Do not touch or approach the sea lions
Do not take marine life
Do not swim in the kelp if it is breaking, because it can hold you down
